title: Strong Nouns (First Declension)
description: Inflect nouns like דָּבָר whose vowels reduce under endings.

blocks.caption: Summary
blocks.html: Nouns whose vowels can change are grouped by how they change when the stress moves. The first family, the strong nouns, looks like the verb perfect: דָּבָר (word), זָקֵן (old man), חָכָם (wise). When an ending is added the stress moves to it, and the vowel two places before it reduces to shewa: דְּבָרִים (words), דְּבַר (word of).

blocks.caption: Three pattern families
blocks.html: Nouns may be arranged by the internal vowel changes produced when the place of the tone shifts through inflection. Words with unchangeable vowels — pure-long or diphthongal — suffer no internal change and need no classification; but the forms with changeable vowels fall into a few clear families. Three of them cover most nouns: the segholates, the strong (verb-like) nouns, and the participial nouns.

blocks.caption: The strong (verb-like) nouns
blocks.html: A large class of nouns has the form of the verb perfect and is chiefly made of participles and adjectives, though many are substantives: דָּבָר (word), חָכָם (wise), קָדוֹשׁ (holy). Their vowels are tone-long and therefore changeable. When the plural ending is added, the tone plants itself on the ending, and the original vowel, now two places from the tone, reduces to shewa: דְּבָרִים (words). The construct is made as short as possible.

blocks.caption: Common confusion
blocks.html: Do not take דְּבַר for a different word from דָּבָר: it is the construct, shortened because it has lost its stress. In the construct plural דִּבְרֵי both vowels have moved.
